newsitem.title: UK: Christies 1996 sales up to 1.02 bln stg. [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Christies 1996 sales up to 1.02 bln stg. [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT]

text.p: British auctioneers Christies International Plc said on Wednesday that its world wide auction sales for 1996 totalled 1.02 billion stg ($1.73 billion), up from 931 millionm stg in the previous year.
Chairman Lord Hindlip said the principal areas of growth were the Asia-Pacific region where sales rose 31 percent, and the United Kingdom where they increased 16 percent.

Christies sold 110 works of art each of which was valued at more than $1.0 million dollars (corrects from one million stg). The most expensive piece of art was Willem de Kooning's Woman, from the Boris Leavitt collection, which was sold for 9.5 million pounds ($16.09 million).
Impressionist & modern art remained the favourite among buyers with the main November sale in New York totalling 50 million stg with 80 percent sold by lot and 95 percent by value.

Christies earned the highest from an Old Master sale in five years at its London sale which realised 20.4 million pounds. The sale's highlight was Raphael's "Study for the head and hand of an apostle" which sold for 5.3 million pounds at its second appearance at Christies.

Among Asian works of art, a Korean iron decorated dragon jar from the Choson dynsty fetched 5.1 million pounds while a Kakiemon model of an Indian elephant in London fethced 749,500 pounds. A collection of Chinese furniture fetched 7.2 million pounds.
Christies sold cars for a value of 10.8 million pounds with a 1949 Ferrari 166 MM Barchetta fetching one million pounds.
A collection of 50 Stutz automobiles sold for 1.3 million pounds.
Wine sales in both London and New York rose 87 percent to 22 million pounds, Christies chairman said.
